A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARC research, despite the changed title and organization. Their algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 and Appendices E-F report original image-classification experiments comparing ARC, unclipped robust aggregation, and static clipping under Byzantine attacks.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds experiments varying model initialization in Section 5.2 and Figures 2b and 6.

M1.justification: ARC retains the same clipping threshold based on the (k+1)-th largest norm, with k=floor(2(f/n)(n-f)). Algorithms 1-3 and the composition with robust aggregation and NNM retain their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 under the same heterogeneity and Byzantine-attack coverage. The new initialization sweep changes model settings within the existing MNIST task.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain CWTM, GM, CWMed, and MK with NNM, static-clipping comparisons, and Byzantine-free DSGD controls. The initialization study uses existing comparison methods; newly cited adaptive-clipping methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 Section 5.2 introduces a controlled sweep multiplying initial parameters by factors 1-5, using CWTM with NNM, ten honest workers, one adversarial worker, and two retained MNIST heterogeneity settings. Existing benchmark protocols and Table 2 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 2b and 6 add sensitivity analysis testing whether ARC's benefits depend on good initialization and when those benefits disappear. Earlier heterogeneity, attack, clipping-threshold, and gradient-norm analyses remain, including those in Appendices E-F.

E5.justification: Appendix D.4 in both versions specifies seeds 1-5 and standard deviations across those five seeds. The additional plots continue this reporting practice without a stated change in repetitions or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New initialization results show ARC accuracy falling from approximately 90% at scaling factor 1 to approximately 10% at factor 5 under extreme heterogeneity (Figure 2b). Table 1's CIFAR-10 values and all earlier plotted results are retained; these are additional findings, not improved scores for the existing benchmarks.

T1.justification: v3 adds the counterexample argument in Lemma C.1 and expands the proof of the previously used output bound into Lemma 5.1. Lemma C.2 replaces v1 Theorem 5.1's maximum-form finite-time bound with a looser additive bound. The principal convergence and breakdown-point results are retained and reorganized.

C1.justification: The central claims of preserving robustness and improving learning under bounded initial gradients remain. v3 adds explicit novelty claims about requiring no additional gradient-distribution knowledge or tuning, and emphasizes that classical aggregators lack ARC's bounded-output property.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the initialization sweep as evidence that ARC exploits favorable initialization, expands discussion of heterogeneity and initialization effects, and adds a theory-versus-practice discussion. v1's explicit qualification as B approaches zero and its proposed differential-privacy extension are omitted.

D1.justification: v3 Section 5.2 identifies PyTorch's default initialization as the starting point and documents the multiplicative scaling procedure. Existing architecture, preprocessing, hyperparameter, and supplementary-material disclosures in Appendix D are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds comparisons with Diakonikolas et al. (2020) and Abdalla and Zhivotovskiy (2024), distinguishing required distribution knowledge and probabilistic guarantees. It also adds heavy-tailed-noise clipping references and removes the dedicated privacy-and-Byzantine-robustness discussion and associated citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Problem formulation and background are merged, empirical evaluation precedes the improved-guarantee discussion, related work becomes a separate late section, and several theoretical statements and qualifications move into Appendix C.

P2.justification: The visual organization changes substantially: v1 Figure 15 becomes v3 Figure 1, earlier main-text panels are regrouped, and two initialization plots are added. Table 1 shortens method labels and bolds ARC scores. The template and appendix layout change throughout; Figure 5's caption partly overflows the bottom of v3 page 7.

improvement.justification: The new initialization sweep provides direct sensitivity evidence for a condition central to v1's theory, while the revised narrative and adaptive-clipping comparisons clarify the contribution. These constitute a focused improvement. Some presentation setbacks remain: the output-norm assumption underlying Lemma 5.1 is less visible in the main text, and Figure 5's caption is partly clipped.
